learn.hook: India has so many festivals that there is something to celebrate almost every month!
points: People of many religions and regions live in India, so we have many festivals.
Diwali is the festival of lights, and Holi is the festival of colours.
Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of the month of Ramzan. Christmas is celebrated on 25 December.
Harvest festivals thank nature for crops: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam, Baisakhi in Punjab and Onam in Kerala.
National festivals belong to every Indian: Republic Day on 26 January, Independence Day on 15 August and Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October.

example.q: Farmers in Tamil Nadu cook rice with milk and jaggery in a new pot to thank the Sun and the cattle for a good crop. Which festival is this?
steps: The clues are: Tamil Nadu, new rice, and thanking nature for a crop.
That makes it a harvest festival of Tamil Nadu.
The festival, and the sweet rice dish too, is called Pongal.

learn.reallife: Look at a calendar at home. Circle the festivals your family celebrates and the ones your friends celebrate!

games.title: Special days through the year
items: Republic Day (26 January)
Independence Day (15 August)
Gandhi Jayanti (2 October)
Children's Day (14 November)

quiz.q: Which festival is called the festival of lights?
quiz.explain: On Diwali, people light diyas and lamps in and around their homes.
steps: On Diwali, people light diyas and lamps.
So Diwali is the festival of lights.
Answer: Diwali
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Diwali and Holi

quiz.q: Which festival is known as the festival of colours?
quiz.explain: On Holi, people play with colours and coloured water.
steps: On Holi, people play with colours.
So Holi is the festival of colours.
Answer: Holi
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Holi with other festivals

quiz.q: On which date do we celebrate Christmas?
quiz.explain: Christmas is celebrated every year on 25 December.
steps: Christmas is celebrated every year on 25 December.
15 August is Independence Day; 26 January is Republic Day.
So the answer is 25 December.
Answer: 25 December
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Christmas with a national festival date

quiz.q: Onam is a harvest festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, with flower pookalams and a big feast.
steps: Onam is a harvest festival.
It is celebrated in Kerala.
So the answer is Kerala.
Answer: Kerala
quiz.mistake: Mixes up harvest festivals of different states

quiz.q: Bihu is a festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated in Assam with music and the lively Bihu dance.
steps: Bihu is a harvest festival with the Bihu dance.
It is celebrated in Assam.
So the answer is Assam.
Answer: Assam
quiz.mistake: Thinks Bihu belongs to Bihar because the names sound alike

quiz.q: Which of these is a national festival celebrated by all Indians?
quiz.explain: Independence Day, on 15 August, is celebrated all over India by everyone.
steps: National festivals belong to every Indian.
Independence Day (15 August) is a national festival.
Pongal, Bihu and Onam are harvest festivals of some states.
So Independence Day is the answer.
Answer: Independence Day
quiz.mistake: Confuses a regional festival with a national festival

quiz.q: Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated at the end of which month?
quiz.explain: Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of Ramzan, the month of fasting.
steps: Eid ul-Fitr comes at the end of the month of Ramzan.
So the answer is Ramzan.
Answer: Ramzan
quiz.mistake: Does not know when Eid ul-Fitr comes

quiz.q: Why are Pongal, Bihu and Baisakhi called harvest festivals?
options: They happen in the rainy night
They are celebrated when crops are ready and gathered
quiz.explain: These festivals celebrate the crops being gathered and thank nature for food.
steps: Pongal, Bihu and Baisakhi thank nature for crops.
They come when crops are ready and gathered.
So they are harvest festivals.
Answer: They are celebrated when crops are ready and gathered
quiz.mistake: Does not know what harvest means

teach.ask: Gappu sees lights one month and colours the next. He asks: why does India have so many festivals?
teach.praise: Tweet! India is like a big garden of festivals!
teach.nudge: Are there festivals for the crops too?

revise.summary: India has many festivals because people of many religions and regions live here. There are festivals like Diwali, Holi, Eid and Christmas, harvest festivals, and national festivals for every Indian.
focus: Main festivals and what they are known for
remember: Diwali = festival of lights; Holi = festival of colours
Christmas = 25 December; Eid ul-Fitr = end of Ramzan
Harvest festivals: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Bihu (Assam), Baisakhi (Punjab), Onam (Kerala)
Republic Day 26 January; Independence Day 15 August; Gandhi Jayanti 2 October
traps: Don't mix up the states: Bihu is Assam, Onam is Kerala.
National festivals belong to all Indians, not one state.

learn.hook: Every festival has a special smell — sweets frying, flowers, fresh paint. Let's explore festival customs!
points: Each festival has special foods. Modaks for Ganesh Chaturthi, sevaiyan for Eid and cake for Christmas.
On Makar Sankranti, people fly kites and eat sweets made of til (sesame) and gur (jaggery).
In Kerala, the Onam feast, called sadya, is served on a banana leaf.
People decorate homes with rangoli, kolam, lights or flowers, and often wear new clothes.
At a gurdwara, people of every background sit together and eat free food at the langar.

example.q: Fatima's family is making sweet vermicelli cooked in milk and greeting neighbours with 'Eid Mubarak'. Which dish is this?
steps: Vermicelli is thin noodle-like strands.
Sweet vermicelli in milk is a favourite festival dish for Eid.
It is called sevaiyan (or sheer khurma).

learn.reallife: Ask your family which special dish they make for a festival, and help them make it with an adult watching.

items.text: Pookalam is made with ___ during Onam.
Free community food at a gurdwara is called ___.
People decorate a tree with stars and lights for ___.

quiz.q: Which sweet is offered during Ganesh Chaturthi?
quiz.explain: Modak, a sweet dumpling with coconut and jaggery, is linked with Ganesh Chaturthi.
steps: Each festival has special foods.
Modaks are made for Ganesh Chaturthi.
So the answer is modak.
Answer: Modak
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival foods

quiz.q: What do people fly on Makar Sankranti?
quiz.explain: Flying kites is a big Makar Sankranti custom, especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
steps: On Makar Sankranti, people fly kites.
So the answer is kites.
Answer: Kites
quiz.mistake: Does not know the kite custom

quiz.q: Til-gur sweets are made from sesame and ___.
quiz.explain: Til means sesame and gur means jaggery. They are mixed to make sweets for Makar Sankranti.
steps: Til-gur sweets are eaten on Makar Sankranti.
Til is sesame; gur is jaggery.
So the answer is jaggery.
Answer: Jaggery
quiz.mistake: Does not know what gur means

quiz.q: On what is the Onam sadya served?
quiz.explain: The Onam feast is served on a banana leaf, a custom from Kerala.
steps: The Onam feast is called sadya.
It is served on a banana leaf.
So the answer is a banana leaf.
Answer: A banana leaf
quiz.mistake: Does not know the sadya custom

quiz.q: What is a langar?
options: Free food served to everyone at a gurdwara
quiz.explain: At the langar, everyone sits together and eats the same food, no matter who they are.
steps: At a gurdwara, everyone sits together to eat.
This free food is called langar.
So a langar is free food served to everyone at a gurdwara.
Answer: Free food served to everyone at a gurdwara
quiz.mistake: Mixes up langar with other customs

quiz.q: Colourful patterns drawn at the doorstep with rice flour or coloured powder are called ___.
quiz.explain: Rangoli and kolam are floor patterns that welcome guests during festivals.
steps: Patterns drawn at the doorstep with rice flour or coloured powder.
These are called rangoli or kolam.
So the answer is rangoli or kolam.
Answer: Rangoli or kolam
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rangoli with mehendi on hands

quiz.q: Which item is used to decorate homes at Christmas?
options: A decorated Christmas tree with a star
quiz.explain: Families decorate a Christmas tree with lights, bells and a star on top.
steps: At Christmas, homes are decorated.
Families decorate a Christmas tree with a star.
So the answer is a decorated Christmas tree with a star.
Answer: A decorated Christmas tree with a star
quiz.mistake: Mixes up decorations of different festivals

quiz.q: Gujiya is a sweet many families make for which festival?
quiz.explain: Gujiya, a sweet stuffed pastry, is popular at Holi in north India.
steps: Gujiya is a sweet stuffed pastry.
Many families make it for Holi.
So the answer is Holi.
Answer: Holi
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival sweets

teach.ask: Gappu wants to join the festival fun. He asks: what special things do people do on festivals?
teach.praise: Chirp! I will make a tiny rangoli with seeds!
teach.nudge: What special food do people make for festivals?

revise.summary: Each festival has special foods and customs, like modaks on Ganesh Chaturthi, til-gur and kites on Makar Sankranti, sadya on a banana leaf at Onam, and langar at a gurdwara.
remember: Modak – Ganesh Chaturthi; sevaiyan – Eid; cake – Christmas; gujiya – Holi
Makar Sankranti: kites and til (sesame) + gur (jaggery) sweets
Onam sadya is served on a banana leaf
Langar = free food for everyone at a gurdwara
traps: Gur means jaggery, not salt or chilli.
Rangoli and kolam are floor patterns, not mehendi.

learn.hook: A festival is more fun with friends! Why do we love celebrating together?
points: Festivals bring families, friends and neighbours together.
People share sweets and greet each other, like 'Happy Diwali' or 'Eid Mubarak'.
Many of us join friends in celebrating their festivals too.
We can celebrate kindly: use natural colours on Holi and keep noise low so pets, birds and elders are not scared.
On national festivals, all of us celebrate together as Indians.

example.q: Neha's neighbour Joseph invites her family for Christmas. Neha's family invites Joseph's family for Diwali. What does this show?
steps: Both families share each other's happy days.
They learn about each other's customs.
This shows friendship and togetherness among neighbours.
example.answer: Festivals help neighbours share joy and come closer

learn.reallife: Your school may celebrate many festivals together in the assembly. Each one is a chance to learn something new.

games.title: Celebrating together
items: We can greet a friend on their festival even if our family does not celebrate it.
Wishing friends on their festival is kind and friendly.
Loud crackers can scare dogs, cats and birds.
Animals have sharp hearing, so loud bangs frighten them.
Throwing colour on someone who says no is good fun.
We should play only with those who want to play.
Republic Day is celebrated by all Indians.
It is a national festival for every Indian.
Sharing sweets with neighbours is a common festival custom.
Many families share sweets with neighbours and friends.
Festivals are only for people of one region.
Many festivals are enjoyed by people from all over India.

games.title: Kind or unkind festival habit?
items: Sharing sweets with neighbours
Using natural Holi colours
Inviting a new friend to join
Helping clean up after a party
Bursting loud crackers near animals
Throwing litter on the road
Leaving out a lonely child
Throwing colour on people who say no

quiz.q: Why do people say festivals bring us together?
options: Families, friends and neighbours celebrate and share joy
quiz.explain: Festivals are times to meet, share food and enjoy together.
steps: During festivals families, friends and neighbours meet.
They celebrate and share joy.
So festivals bring us together.
Answer: Families, friends and neighbours celebrate and share joy
quiz.mistake: Does not see the social side of festivals

quiz.q: Your friend Harpreet celebrates Gurpurab. What is a friendly thing to do?
options: Tell her it is not a real festival
quiz.explain: Wishing friends on their festivals shows respect and friendship.
steps: We can join friends in their festivals.
Wishing her a happy Gurpurab shows respect.
So that is the friendly thing to do.
Answer: Wish her a happy Gurpurab
quiz.mistake: Does not respect other people's festivals

quiz.q: Why should we avoid very loud crackers?
options: They scare animals and disturb babies and elders
quiz.explain: Loud bangs frighten animals and can trouble babies, elders and sick people. Smoke also dirties the air.
steps: Loud crackers make big bangs.
They scare animals and disturb babies and elders.
So we should avoid very loud crackers.
Answer: They scare animals and disturb babies and elders
quiz.mistake: Does not think about others who are affected

quiz.q: Which is a nature-friendly way to play Holi?
options: Use paint from the shop wall
Use colours made from flowers and turmeric
quiz.explain: Natural colours from flowers, leaves and turmeric are gentler on skin and nature.
steps: We can celebrate Holi kindly with natural colours.
Colours from flowers and turmeric are gentle on skin and nature.
So that is the nature-friendly way.
Answer: Use colours made from flowers and turmeric
quiz.mistake: Thinks any colour is safe to use

quiz.q: On Independence Day, schools hoist the national flag. Who celebrates this day?
quiz.explain: Independence Day is a national festival for every Indian, everywhere.
steps: Independence Day is a national festival.
It belongs to every Indian.
So all Indians celebrate it.
Answer: All Indians
quiz.mistake: Thinks national festivals belong to only some people

quiz.q: What do people often say to each other on Eid?
quiz.explain: 'Eid Mubarak' means 'blessed Eid'. People hug and greet each other with these words.
steps: On Eid people greet each other.
They say 'Eid Mubarak'.
So the answer is Eid Mubarak.
Answer: Eid Mubarak
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festival greetings

quiz.q: After the colony Diwali party, the park is full of wrappers. What should the children do?
options: Help clean up and put waste in dustbins
Hide the wrappers under the swings
quiz.explain: Celebrating together also means cleaning up together.
steps: After the party, the park has wrappers.
Celebrating together means cleaning up together.
So help clean up and put waste in dustbins.
Answer: Help clean up and put waste in dustbins
quiz.mistake: Thinks someone else will always clean up

quiz.q: Which of these shows togetherness during a festival?
options: Eating alone and hiding the sweets
quiz.explain: Sharing food with neighbours brings people closer.
steps: Togetherness means sharing joy with others.
Sharing food with neighbours brings people closer.
So sharing food with neighbours shows togetherness.
Answer: Sharing food with neighbours
quiz.mistake: Confuses selfish actions with celebration

teach.ask: Gappu's neighbours are celebrating a festival he does not know. He asks: can I join them? Why do festivals matter?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! I will wish my neighbours and share my seeds!
teach.nudge: What can I share with my neighbours on a festival?

revise.summary: Festivals bring families, friends and neighbours together to share joy and food. We celebrate kindly by using natural colours, keeping noise low and cleaning up together.
focus: Celebrating in ways kind to nature, animals and elders
remember: Keep noise low so pets, birds and elders are not scared
National festivals are celebrated by all Indians together
traps: Loud crackers are not harmless; they scare animals and disturb babies and elders.
Don't leave litter after a party; clean up together.
